addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum i: four directions to improve prediction (longer horizons, an event calendar, a sales target, intent signals)
parent_record: prereg/wiki_led_settings_2026-10-20.json and addenda a to h; their settings apply unless changed here
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who asked on 22 Oct (00:10 to 00:20) to widen the prediction window from one month to quarters, years or specific frames, and to test an event calendar, a sales target and intent signals now: 'test multiple things and directions to see what is the best way possible'
status: Exploratory: four directions compared by fixed measures, all reported; no direction is chosen after looking at results without saying so. Every interval is a 95% interval.

D1_horizons_books.rows: Test A's corrected rows (data/db/wiki_led/test_a_rows_c.parquet: the 7,747 works with their own English article; Test A's corrected Wikipedia and library features; Test A's training and test years and seed).
D1_horizons_books.targets: For horizon k in 1, 3, 6 and 12 months: the Test A change target applied to the mean monthly loans of months t+1 to t+k (k = 1 is Test A), and 'rose' = that mean at least 1.5 times the six-month median M6 (Test A's rule with the mean in place of next month). A row needs all k months observed (excluded months as in Test A); rows whose window ends after the last month are dropped.
D1_horizons_books.models: Test A's three LightGBM models and settings, refit for each k: W (Wikipedia features only), H (library history only), HW (both); plus the persistence rule. Nothing is tuned.
D1_horizons_books.measures: Mean within-origin-month Spearman of predicted and actual change (Test A's measure, month-block bootstrap), the top-20 share that rose per month, and the added value HW minus H. Main comparison: does the added value of Wikipedia (HW minus H) and W's own skill grow from k = 1 to k = 3, 6, 12? Reported for every k with intervals; descriptive.

D1_horizons_themes.no_fitting_ranking: The Wikipedia-only theme ranking of Test C and G3 (monthly change of a theme's attention series, ranked within origin, format and level against the change in borrowing) with the borrowing change measured over the next 1, 3, 6 and 12 months (mean log share of months t+1 to t+k minus month t), for S2 (all AI pages), S2C (AI concept pages) and the hand-checked concept pages (cur_wlog), on the benchmark's main rows (print and ebook).
D1_horizons_themes.event_windows: For lasting rises (4 weeks or more) of S2C, S2 and the hand-checked concept pages, the effect on borrowing in months 3 to 5 and 6 to 11 and over months 0 to 11, against the synthetic control and the own trend, panel a, both levels pooled, with the settings of addendum g. Descriptive. If the event code cannot be extended by 22 Oct 18:00, only the no-fitting ranking is reported and the report says so.

D2_event_calendar.events: data/db/wiki_led/events.parquet (Wikidata, fetched 20 Oct for the 7,747 works): film and television adaptation releases (month precision), the author's death, dated awards. The date is assumed known in advance for releases and known from its month for deaths and awards; Wikidata entries may have been added later, which is a limit, said in the report.
D2_event_calendar.event_study: Loans of each work in months -3 to +12 around its event, relative to its six-month median before the event, against works with no event in the same months and of similar loan level (matched within origin month and loan decile). Excess share that rose (1.5 times M6) and surged (2 times and 5 loans or more) by month and by event type.
D2_event_calendar.prediction: At each origin month t, the alert list of works with an adaptation release in months t+1 to t+3 (and, separately, deaths and awards in month t): the share that rose and surged in months t+1 to t+3 against the base rate, against the library model's top picks (Test A's H), and whether adding these works to H's top 20 raises its hit rate. The improvement round v2 (dated events as model features, no gain over the same dates moved 12 months) is reported beside.

D3_sales_target.data: New York Times best-seller lists, weekly, June 2008 to October 2026 (data/collectors/nyt, the official Books API, 959 weekly files already collected). Books matched to the Seattle works by ISBN-13 (NYT primary and listed ISBNs against the Seattle records), else by normalised title and author family name; the match rate is reported.
D3_sales_target.tests: (a) Among matched works not on any NYT list in month t, does Wikipedia (Test A's W features) rank which appear on a list in month t+1 (AUC and top-20 share), against the library model H, HW and chance? (b) Lead and lag: within work, the correlation of monthly changes in Seattle loans with NYT presence 1 to 3 months earlier and later. (c) Seattle loans after a work's first NYT week (event study as D2). Descriptive with intervals.

D4_intent_collection: Open Library reading-log counts (want to read, currently reading, already read) for the Test A works and the 20,000 Test F books, mapped by Wikidata P648 (Open Library ID) and, where missing, the Open Library search API by ISBN; a weekly snapshot from 22 Oct 2026 by a scheduled collector, at most 1 request a second with the project user agent. No analysis now: its history starts now. Google Trends is not collected by program until official API access exists.
time_rule: Results reported on 22 Oct 2026 by 20:00 +07 for the meeting of 23 Oct; a direction not finished by then is reported as not done.
seen_before_fixing: All results of Tests A to F and addendum h; the 20 Oct exploratory check of Test A two months ahead (library 0.336, Wikipedia 0.138, 2019 to 2023); the improvement round v2 (dated events gained as much with dates moved 12 months); the NYT collection exists, but in the Wikipedia-led tests NYT lists have not been matched to the Seattle works or related to Wikipedia or loans. No D1 to D3 result exists.
